title: Over 30% of arrest warrant requests rejected by prosecutors this year: data
bullets: Prosecutors rejected 34.1 percent of police arrest warrant requests between January and August of this year, surpassing 30 percent for the first time.
The rejection rate for arrest warrants has increased steadily since 2021, accompanied by complaints from police investigators.
Prosecutors also rejected 19.1 percent of police requests for search and seizure warrants during the same period.

title: Police officer arrested for fabricating, distributing sexually exploitative images
bullets: A police officer from Seoul's Dongdaemun Police Station was formally arrested last month for possessing, fabricating, and distributing sexually exploitative images.
A forensic analysis of his mobile phone revealed thousands of files, including deepfake images, child sexual exploitation materials, and illegally filmed images.
The officer has been relieved of duty while the investigation continues.

title: (Asiad) Celtic winger Yang Hyun-jun lauded for mentorship in S. Korea's run to men's football gold
bullets: South Korea's head coach Lee Min-sung chose injured winger Yang Hyun-jun as his personal MVP after winning the men's football gold medal at the Asian Games.
Yang Hyun-jun played in only one match against Qatar before aggravating a hamstring injury that sidelined him for the rest of the tournament.
Yang Hyun-jun helped his younger roommate, Yang Min-hyeok, stay focused and overcome pressure during the competition.

title: Over 30 pct of arrest warrant requests rejected by prosecutors this year: data
bullets: Prosecutors rejected over 30 percent of police arrest warrant requests between January and August, reaching 34.1 percent.
Police investigators believe prosecutors are hesitating to seek warrants because of a major overhaul that stripped prosecutors of investigative powers.
South Korea recently abolished the traditional prosecution office and launched two new agencies to separate investigation and indictment powers.

title: Seoul police officer detained over AI sexual deepfakes, thousands of illegal files
bullets: A serving Seoul police officer from the Dongdaemun Police Station was detained for allegedly creating and distributing AI-generated sexual deepfakes and possessing thousands of illegal files.
Busan police uncovered the crimes through an undercover Telegram investigation that began after obtaining court approval in December 2025.
A forensic search of the officer's devices revealed about 5,600 illegal files, including child sexual exploitation material, illegally filmed videos, and fabricated nude images of acquaintances.

title: Shark returns to canal a day after 2nd rescue attempt
bullets: A 3.5-meter shark named Bukang-i returned to a canal in Busan after getting past a net installed by authorities to guide it to the open sea.
The rescue operation was halted after the net became stuck to the bottom of the canal and the shark refused to move out.
The shark has attracted over 700,000 visitors since it was first spotted in the canal on September 18 and was named an honorary ambassador of Busan.

The K-Pop news section highlights an October comeback lineup for the fall weather, alongside content like Wonder Hours with Hyerim.

title: Park Geun-hye releases letter written by her late father amid film controversy
bullets: Representative Yoo Young-ha released a handwritten letter written by former President Park Chung-hee in 1974 following criticism of the film "The Assassin(s)."
The letter was written to Park Geun-hye two days after the death of her mother, first lady Yuk Young-soo.
Yoo demanded that the film be pulled, asked the producers to apologize, and stated he is considering legal action.

title: Dispute intensifies over police search of pediatric emergency room
bullets: Police searched the pediatric emergency center at Ajou University Hospital following the death of a four-month-old infant who could not be saved after being transferred there.
Medical groups strongly criticized the police action, warning that searching active emergency rooms disrupts critical patient care and increases doctors' fears of criminal liability.
Police stated they executed the search under a court warrant to quickly secure evidence, while doctors called for clear standards to limit investigative disruptions in emergency settings.

title: Sayuwon's first music festival opens with moonlight performance of Beethoven's 'Pastoral'
bullets: Sayuwon, a mountain garden in Daegu, hosted its first music festival from September 18 to 20, opening with a moonlight performance of Beethoven's "Pastoral."
The festival's outdoor venue, Symphony 6, is a purpose-built acoustic structure designed by Italian architect Andrea Liverani featuring an origami-like canopy of weathering steel.
Developed by Yoo Jae-sung and opened in 2021, the sprawling garden has gained popularity among architecture and landscape enthusiasts.

title: [Breaking] North Korea fires unidentified projectile toward East Sea: JCS
bullets: North Korea fired an unidentified projectile toward the East Sea on Saturday, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff.
The military detected the launch in the morning without immediately releasing details regarding the type, number, or flight distance of the projectile.
The launch occurred a day after Kim Yo-jong reiterated Pyongyang's decision to cut off ties with Seoul and rejected a proposal for talks.

title: Busan shark's second rescue attempt ends without success
bullets: Authorities in Busan failed in their second attempt to guide a 3.5-meter shark out of an artificial canal using a large net.
Officials decided to leave the net in place and wait for the shark to swim out on its own after it refused to move toward the exit.
The shark, nicknamed Bukang, was first spotted in the canal on September 18 and has since drawn over 600,000 visitors to the waterfront park.

title: Galaxy S27 prices could rise more than planned after S26 price increase
bullets: Samsung Electronics might raise prices for the upcoming Galaxy S27 series more than initially planned due to surging DRAM and NAND flash costs.
According to a tech leaker, the additional price increase for the S27 could reach around $100 and vary based on storage capacity.
Samsung recently increased prices for its current Galaxy S26 lineup in Korea and the US following a mid-cycle cost adjustment.

title: Seoul looks to foreign entrepreneurs to fuel its next economic engine
bullets: A Ukrainian entrepreneur won Seoul's second annual Jump Up, Start Up competition with an AI platform that predicts fall risks for the elderly.
The winning startup received a cash reward and thirty points toward South Korea's D-8-4 technology startup visa.
Seoul is supporting foreign entrepreneurs to help drive economic growth as the country faces plummeting birth rates and slowing growth.

title: Civic group to rally outside actor's home over film 'The Assassin(s)'
bullets: A conservative civic group plans to hold daily protests outside the home of actor Yoo Hae-jin starting Saturday.
The group is protesting alleged historical inaccuracies in Yoo's film "The Assassin(s)," which deals with the 1974 assassination of former first lady Yuk Young-soo.
The group's leader stated they want Yoo to appear in right-wing movies to achieve political balance.

title: (Asiad) Esports legend Faker tells children to play games in moderation
bullets: Esports star Lee Sang-hyeok, known as Faker, advised young gamers to find passions and maintain healthy habits to avoid excessive addiction.
South Korea won its second straight Asian Games gold medal in League of Legends by defeating Chinese Taipei 3-0 in Japan.
Although Faker did not play in the final match, he expressed no regrets and praised his teammates for their hard work and tenacity.

title: A movie about a first lady's murder has Korea's conservatives fuming. Now its stars are paying the price
bullets: A South Korean journalism thriller titled "The Assassin(s)" has sparked intense political uproar among conservatives for suggesting a former president may have been involved in his wife's 1974 assassination.
The film's production company announced that the cast and director will skip the upcoming Busan International Film Festival and canceled a public screening due to safety concerns.
Stars of the movie, including Lee Min-ho and Yoo Hae-jin, have faced boycotts, withdrawal from festival events, and pressure from angry social media users.

title: (Asiad) Men's football team goes for 4th straight title as medal race winds down
bullets: South Korea will play against Japan in the men's football final on Saturday in pursuit of their fourth consecutive Asian Games gold medal.
The South Korean under-23 team features European-based attackers such as Eom Ji-sung, Lee Young-jun, and Bae Jun-ho.
South Korean athletes will also compete for gold medals on Saturday in archery, taekwondo, sport climbing, and men's golf.

title: For Tom Cruise, films are reflection of humanity
bullets: Hollywood star Tom Cruise visited South Korea to promote his latest film, "Digger," marking his 13th official trip to the country.
In "Digger," directed by Alejandro Gonzalez Inarritu, Cruise plays a stubborn oil tycoon whose actions lead to a global catastrophe.
Cruise stated that he aims to absorb and reflect humanity in his films to let audiences see themselves in the stories.

title: 59 hospitalized after chlorine gas spreads in Jeju hotel
bullets: Fifty-nine people were hospitalized after chlorine gas spread through a hotel on Jeju Island.
The gas formed because pool disinfectants were apparently mixed at the wrong ratio during cleaning.
Guests suffered symptoms like nausea and dizziness, but none had serious injuries.

title: Some 25,000 customers' info leaked from Shinhan Bank in apparent AI agent-assisted hacking
bullets: Shinhan Bank reported that a hacking attack leaked the personal information of about 25,000 customers.
Overseas hackers allegedly used advanced artificial intelligence tools to carry out the attack.
The Financial Supervisory Service sent a team to conduct an on-site inspection regarding the data leak.

title: (Asiad) Sport climber Seo Chae-hyun wins bronze for 2nd straight medal
bullets: Sport climber Seo Chae-hyun won the bronze medal in the women's boulder event at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan.
Seo finished with 70 points and won a tiebreaker against China's Luo Zhilu based on her higher score in the semifinals.
Zhang Yuetong of China won the gold medal and Ai Mori of Japan took the silver medal.

title: University of Seoul's Extracurricular Festa offers hands-on extracurricular experiences
bullets: The University of Seoul hosted its 6th Extracurricular Festa on campus on September 22 to give students hands-on access to various extracurricular programs.
The annual event featured 20 booths covering areas like academic majors, careers, and employment, alongside an awards ceremony and a prize drawing.
University President Won Yong-kul stated that the institution will continue strengthening student-centered learning and practical experience through these programs.

title: Unification ministry reaffirms peaceful coexistence policy despite DMZ blast
bullets: South Korea's unification ministry stated it will continue pursuing peaceful coexistence with North Korea despite a recent land mine blast inside the Demilitarized Zone.
The explosion injured three South Korean soldiers, prompting the military to blame North Korea and demand an apology for violating the Armistice Agreement.
Unification Minister Chung Dong-young cut short his European work trip to return home and manage the aftermath of the incident.

title: Gender equality minister says presidential office asked her to 'steady' ministry
bullets: Gender Equality Minister Won Min-kyong stated that the presidential office asked her to steady her ministry following a withdrawal by a nominee to replace her.
Won plans to work with her staff to steadfastly push for policy tasks previously reported to the president and the public.
The ministry recently launched a free public sanitary pad program in 12 municipalities and plans to expand it nationwide next year.

title: President keeps NK dialogue push amid DMZ mine dispute
bullets: President Lee Jae Myung stated that South Korea will keep trying to lower military tensions with North Korea and urged Pyongyang to return to dialogue.
The remarks followed an investigation blaming North Korean land mines for a DMZ explosion on September 21 that left three South Korean service members injured.
Lee also reaffirmed plans to pursue the transfer of wartime operational control and to create a unified military academy.

title: BTS becomes first pop group to surpass $500 m in tour ticket sales
bullets: Global K-pop group BTS has become the first pop group in the world to surpass $500 million in cumulative ticket sales with its "Arirang" world tour.
Billboard reported that BTS is the seventh group overall to reach this milestone, while noting that the other six ensembles are rock bands.
Billboard projected that the tour could ultimately generate $1 billion in cumulative revenue with around 40 concerts still scheduled.

The annual festival featured twenty booths, an awards ceremony for outstanding departments and student teams, and a prize drawing.
University President Won Yong-kul stated that the school will continue to strengthen practical experience and build a student-centered education system.

title: Korea tracks passports to stop improper welfare payouts to families overseas
bullets: South Korea is linking its social security network with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs passport database to stop improper child-welfare payouts to families living overseas.
Children born abroad who entered Korea on temporary passports previously avoided automatic tracking, allowing families to receive welfare benefits during long-term stays outside the country.
The new real-time system automatically alerts local officials when temporary passports are issued, reducing administrative waste and the need to claw back misallocated funds.

title: BTS becomes 1st pop group to surpass US$500 mln in tour ticket sales
bullets: BTS has become the first pop group in the world to surpass US$500 million in cumulative ticket sales with its "Arirang" world tour.
In August alone, the group staged 12 concerts that drew about 800,000 fans and generated $171.7 million in ticket sales.
Billboard projected that the ongoing tour could ultimately generate $1 billion in cumulative revenue with around 40 concerts still scheduled.

title: Indonesian film remake of ‘Descendants of the Sun’ to debut in 2027
bullets: An Indonesian film remake of the hit K-drama "Descendants of the Sun" is scheduled to debut in theaters in 2027 in both Indonesia and South Korea.
The film is directed by Hanung Bramantyo and stars Reza Rahadian and Dian Sastrowardoyo in the lead roles.
South Korean production company Next Entertainment World is participating in the planning and co-production of the remake, which has already wrapped filming.

title: Lebanese traditional dance troupe tours Korea for 19th Arab Culture Festival
bullets: Lebanese dance troupe Hayakel Baalbeck is touring South Korea from September 5 to 10 to mark 45 years of diplomatic relations and the Arab Culture Festival.
Organized by the Embassy of Lebanon, the group's performances in Seoul, Gwangju, and Gyeongju combine traditional Lebanese dabke dance with Korean music.
Lebanese Ambassador Wael Hachem stated that cultural exchanges help build genuine friendship between the people of both nations beyond formal government agreements.

title: Historic hanok sets stage for Dream Forest concert in nothern Seoul
bullets: Seoul is holding an autumn music festival on Saturday at the historic Changnyeong Wigung Jaesa hanok complex in Dream Forest.
The festival offers food trucks and five paid craft activities for up to 800 participants on a first-come, first-served basis.
A free outdoor concert featuring various musical performances will begin at 5:30 p.m. with no advance reservation required.

title: Lisa says she hid past relationships as K-pop star
bullets: Blackpink's Lisa revealed in her upcoming documentary that she had to hide past relationships to protect her group's popularity.
She wrote the song "Dream" from her solo album about one of these private relationships after obtaining the person's permission.
Her documentary "Always Lalisa" will make its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11.

title: New head coach for men's nat'l football team promises 'work, honesty, respect'
bullets: The Korea Football Association has appointed Spanish tactician Robert Moreno as the temporary head coach of the South Korean men's national football team.
Moreno will oversee the team for six matches through November 27, with an opportunity to stay on for the Asian Cup depending on his performance.
In a post on his website, Moreno promised to deliver work, honesty, and respect in his new position rather than guaranteeing results.

title: Interim Korea coach vows to let football do the talking
bullets: Roberto Moreno has been appointed as the interim manager of the South Korean men's national football team, becoming the country's first Spanish head coach.
He signed a three-month contract for six matches, which includes an option to stay through next year's Asian Cup depending on the team's performance.
Moreno fills the vacancy left by Hong Myung-bo and will lead his first game against Ecuador on September 24.

title: Naver founder, Brookfield chief meet for follow-up talks on AI factory
bullets: Naver founder Lee Hae-jin met with Brookfield CEO Bruce Flatt to discuss advancing a 1 gigawatt AI factory project.
Brookfield agreed to invest up to $9 billion in the project's 200-megawatt first phase through a special purpose entity.
Nvidia is also participating in the project through an agreement to acquire common shares in Naver.

title: Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics win 11 innovation awards at IFA 2026
bullets: Samsung Electronics and LG Electronics won a combined total of 11 awards at the IFA 2026 tech trade show in Berlin.
Samsung received four innovation awards, with its Bespoke wall-mounted air conditioner recognized in both the design and home appliances categories.
LG won seven product awards, which included the event's top honor of best brand.

title: On this day in Korea - September 4, 1994: Taekwondo becomes Olympic sport
bullets: On September 4, 1994, delegates at the 103rd IOC Congress in Paris voted to approve Taekwondo as an official Olympic medal sport.
The martial art emphasizes speed, agility, high-kicking techniques, and disciplined mental strength.
Becoming an Olympic sport helped elevate Korea's national sport into a global discipline practiced by millions of people worldwide.

title: Sungkyunkwan University team develops nanocomposite material with enhanced thermal conductivity
bullets: Sungkyunkwan University researchers developed a new nanocomposite material with enhanced electrical and thermal conductivity.
Unlike conventional materials, this material's thermal conductivity actually increases when it is stretched.
The research team successfully applied this new material to heat-dissipation technology for foldable smartphones.

title: Will foreign residents qualify for Korea’s $370 marriage subsidy?
bullets: Starting in 2027, South Korea plans to provide a combined 1 million won cash subsidy to couples who register a marriage. This program will replace an existing marriage tax credit.
Although foreign residents were eligible for the previous tax credit, the government has not yet decided if they will qualify for the new cash subsidy.
The initiative faces criticism from unmarried individuals, LGBTQ+ groups, and non-traditional households who argue the policy excludes them.

title: Movie theaters must provide audio, visual aids for people with disabilities: Supreme Court
bullets: South Korea's Supreme Court ruled that movie theaters must provide audio and visual assistance for people with visual or hearing impairments.
The court overturned an appellate ruling that had limited the required assistance to auditoriums with at least 300 seats and only 3 percent of screenings.
Four plaintiffs with disabilities originally filed the lawsuit in 2016 against major theater chains CGV, Lotte Cultureworks, and Megabox JoongAng.

title: Seoul shares extend gains late Thu. morning as oil prices ease
bullets: South Korea's benchmark stock index rose 1.4 percent late Thursday morning, recovering from a steep drop in the previous session.
Shares gained as oil prices eased after U.S. President Donald Trump said renewed attacks on Iran would likely be short-lived.
Major South Korean companies, including Samsung Electronics, Hyundai Motor, and LG Energy Solution, saw their stock prices increase.

title: Daewoong steps up cooperation with Indonesia
bullets: A delegation from Indonesia's food and drug regulator visited Daewoong Pharmaceutical's Magok Research Center in Seoul.
Both sides discussed potential partnerships regarding product development, drug approvals, and regulatory affairs in Indonesia.
Daewoong has maintained Indonesia as a strategic base for its global pharmaceutical business for more than 20 years.

title: Labor ministry's new guidelines exclude profit-linked bonus demands from mandatory bargaining
bullets: South Korea's labor ministry issued new guidelines stating that demands for performance bonuses tied to a fixed percentage of company profits are not mandatory bargaining subjects.
The guidelines also establish that company decisions regarding major new projects, such as Samsung's planned semiconductor plants, cannot be forcibly negotiated unless personnel restructuring occurs.
The ministry provided these rules to resolve confusion caused by a revised trade union law that took effect in March.

title: S. Korea says respects 'One China' policy amid Taiwan Pavilion dispute
bullets: China's pavilion team withdrew from the Gwangju Biennale to protest the use of the name "Taiwan Pavilion."
South Korea's foreign ministry reaffirmed its respect for the "One China" policy, noting that the naming decision was made independently by the private art sector.
The South Korean government stated that it hopes the dispute will not harm its relations or cooperation with China.

title: Nat'l football body opens disciplinary case against referee over alleged remark on player
bullets: The Korea Football Association opened disciplinary proceedings against referee Bae Sun-young for allegedly making a sexually harassing comment about a player.
Player Ji So-yun accused Bae of saying she must be on her period, and stated that the referee gave her a yellow card after being confronted.
Bae claimed her comment was not directed at any specific player, while the football association promised to prepare measures to prevent similar incidents.

title: 6 missing, 1 dead after tugboat capsizes off Busan
bullets: A tugboat carrying eight crew members capsized and sank off the coast of Busan.
One crew member died, one was rescued, and six others remain missing.
Authorities deployed vessels and aircraft to search for the missing crew, but strong waves and currents are hampering the operation.

title: Intensive search under way for 9 S. Koreans missing in Nepal floods
bullets: A 44-member South Korean disaster relief team arrived in Nepal to help search for victims missing after massive floods and landslides.
Nine South Koreans went missing on August 26 while working at a hydropower plant construction site in Nepal's Rasuwa district.
South Korea is providing rescue dogs, advanced search equipment, DNA testing tools, and approximately 38,000 blankets to support the relief efforts.

title: Number of Foreign Workers under Permit System Hits Fresh Record
bullets: A video featured multiple K-pop artists, including NCT 127 and ENHYPEN, on their way to Music Bank on August 28, 2026.
A feature titled "Wonder Hours with Hyerim" listed ten reasons to date AxMxP on August 26, 2026.
A K-POP News segment published on August 31, 2026, highlighted music comebacks scheduled for September.

title: Hyundai cooling film takes heat off police buses
bullets: Hyundai Motor Group installed its transparent Nano Cooling Film on two Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency buses.
The film reflects solar heat and releases interior heat, keeping the bus interior about 2 to 3 degrees Celsius cooler on average.
Hyundai plans to monitor the buses for one year before deciding whether to start full-scale production.

title: Gyeonggi support center aids over 700 migrant women in 1st year after opening
bullets: Between August 2025 and June 2026, the Gyeonggi Foreign Women’s Counseling Center provided 6,101 counseling sessions to 712 migrant women.
The center assists foreign women facing domestic abuse, legal anxieties, and financial stress, operating regardless of their immigration status.
Provincial leaders plan to expand counseling hubs into northern Gyeonggi and recruit interpreters for rare dialects to improve accessibility.

title: Lee orders to mobilize all available resources to search, rescue crew of capsized tugboat
bullets: A 286-ton tugboat carrying eight crew members capsized off the coast of Busan on Wednesday afternoon.
Rescuers saved two crew members, leaving one unconscious, while six others remain missing.
President Lee Jae Myung and Prime Minister Han Seong-sook ordered all available resources to be mobilized for the rescue efforts.

title: Voice phishing crimes drop 40 pct thanks to tougher measures
bullets: The government implemented special measures to fight voice phishing, such as emergency phone number blocking, AI warning systems, and international cooperation.
Voice phishing cases continuously declined for 10 consecutive months from October to July, falling 39.9 percent on-year to 12,554 cases.
Financial losses from voice phishing crimes dropped 43.2 percent to 632.4 billion won during the same period.

title: Veterans ministry seeks 8 pct hike in 2027 budget for expanded honors, key projects
bullets: South Korea's Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs has proposed a 7.22 trillion won budget for next year, representing an 8 percent increase.
The plan expands financial benefits for war veterans and independence fighters' descendants while lowering the age threshold for using veterans hospitals from 75 to 65.
The proposed budget will also fund turning Hyochang Park into a national cemetery and preparing for the 2029 Invictus Games in Daejeon.

title: Cortis’ ‘Redred’ best K-pop song this summer: TikTok
bullets: Cortis' song "Redred" topped TikTok's Songs of the Summer 2026 list for Korea, and the group was named Boyband of the Summer.
The track is the lead single from their second EP "Greengreen," which entered the Billboard 200 chart at No. 3.
Cortis is scheduled to perform three concerts in Yokohama, Japan, starting Friday for their "Put Your Phone Down" tour.

title: 2 rescued, 6 missing after tugboat capsizes in waters off Busan
bullets: A 286-ton tugboat carrying eight crew members capsized in the waters off Busan on Wednesday afternoon.
Two crew members have been rescued so far, while six others remain missing.
President Lee Jae Myung instructed authorities to mobilize all available resources for search and rescue operations.

title: Korea moves to protect migrant fishermen from forced labor
bullets: South Korea's government issued updated guidelines to help law enforcement identify and protect migrant fishermen from forced labor and human trafficking.
The new framework sets clear warning signs of physical, emotional, and financial coercion tailored specifically to the maritime fishing industry.
Officials aim to use these rules to spot labor abuses at ports before ships leave for isolated waters.

title: Korea overhauls child protection system after death of 11-year-old
bullets: South Korea announced a major overhaul of its child protection system after an 11-year-old disabled child died from fatal abuse.
The new guidelines require police and local child protection officers to share real-time report details and perform mandatory joint site visits.
The government will automatically prioritize removing a child from any household that receives two or more abuse reports within a year.

title: Korea seeks to toughen pension eligibility for foreign residents as loophole found
bullets: South Korea is tightening its national pension rules for foreign residents after a loophole allowed them to secure benefits through lump-sum retroactive payments.
A government investigation identified three foreign applicants who used this back-payment scheme, but only one is currently receiving a pension.
Under new regulations, retroactive payments are only allowed for months in which a foreign resident stayed in South Korea for at least 15 days.

title: Court approves corporate rehabilitation plan for Homeplus
bullets: A Seoul court approved a corporate rehabilitation plan for Homeplus Co. after creditors and shareholders voted in favor of it.
The discount store chain previously filed for rehabilitation due to liquidity concerns and a declining credit rating.
Under the approved plan, Homeplus aims to sell 19 closed stores by February 2028 to repay debts totaling 1.3 trillion won.

title: Busan film festival unveils 315-film lineup for 31st edition
bullets: The 31st Busan International Film Festival will screen 315 films from 59 countries, making it the festival's largest lineup since 2019.
The festival is now an Oscar-qualifying event, allowing the winner of its best film award to qualify for the Oscar for best international feature.
This year's edition places a major focus on animation and will host international guests including Michelle Yeoh and Maggie Gyllenhaal.

title: South Korea’s Oceans Ministry unveils record 2027 budget to drive maritime growth
bullets: South Korea’s Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries has proposed a record 82.6 trillion won budget for 2027. This represents a 10.8 percent increase from the previous year.
The proposed funds will be used for port infrastructure development, smart aquaculture, artificial intelligence cargo systems, and marine technology research.
Environmental programs in the plan focus on fighting illegal fishing, using robotic systems to collect marine waste, and expanding coastal carbon storage projects.

title: S. Korea dispatches disaster relief team to Nepal to support flood recovery efforts
bullets: South Korea dispatched a 44-person disaster relief team to Nepal to support search and rescue efforts following severe floods. The team will stay in Nepal for about 10 days to help locate victims using specialized equipment and search dogs.

The massive floods and mudslides in Nepal killed over 800 people and left nine South Korean power plant workers missing in Rasuwa district. A South Korean rapid response team is already on the ground conducting joint searches with the Nepali military.

Rescue workers recently recovered one unidentified body from a tunnel at the hydropower plant site where the missing South Koreans were working. Officials are currently working through diplomatic channels to confirm the identity and nationality of the victim.
